accuracy.reason: All nine objectives accurately distinguish replicated copies from shards, snapshot/log handoff, receipt/durability/application acknowledgments, lag and read routing, topology and safe failover, historical recovery and scoped policy. Live primary documents support the critical stages and failure limits.

mechanisms.reason: The stack traces initial copy through ordered log receipt and replay, then connects acknowledgment timing to lost-write windows, lag to old reads, silence to split brain and fencing, and replicated deletions to historical restore. Diagrams match each process.

evidence.quote: Receiving a change and applying it are separate steps.

coherence.reason: Purpose and propagation precede async/sync choices, lag, topology, failover, backup and operational policy. All prerequisite terms are introduced and examples support their immediate mechanisms without requiring one continuous story.

evidence.quote: Replication keeps copies of the same data. Sharding divides data into different groups.

decisions.reason: The learner can choose ack stage/count and read routing from freshness/loss/latency targets, separate safe takeover from copy existence, and retain/test recovery history. Costs include write waits, replica dependence, load, storage and network work.

evidence.quote: Choose acceptable acknowledged-write loss, read freshness, write latency and recovery time before choosing replica settings.

clarity.reason: Snapshot, log, stages, topology, fencing and recovery terms are explicitly defined. The dense nine-card stack remains sufficient for the basic audience; implementation-specific eligibility and fencing commands are outside the contract. Diagram/UI source inspected, not executed.

evidence.quote: A fixed sleep or low average lag is not proof that a particular write is visible.

outcomes.reason: Learner distinguishes copied versus divided data, read/recovery benefits and their routing/coordination limits, snapshot/log alignment/order, and receipt versus application.
Learner traces async acknowledgment then permanent writer loss and contrasts configured sync replica count/stages, remote wait costs, unavailable replicas and bounded protection.

Learner explains lag stage and own-write visibility, authoritative primary or specific applied-write checks with load/delay/failover limits, stale-tolerant reads, and all three topologies with conflict/repair obligations.

Learner defines failover/promotion/split brain, uncertain silence, candidate progress, fencing and routing; covers async loss, propagated mistakes, backups/log retention and usable timed restore tests.

Learner clarifies unsupplied loss/freshness/latency/recovery targets and proposes a supported durable-ack/replica-read policy, safe failover, historical tested backup and progress/health/write-wait monitoring, without promising zero loss/downtime.

sourceChecks.claim: Live RDS read-replica documentation supports copied data and explicit query routing for read scaling, not automatic writer scaling or takeover.

Live PostgreSQL logical-replication documentation distinguishes physical block from logical data changes, snapshot initialization and same-order ongoing application. Initial copy and log position must describe a consistent handoff.
Live PostgreSQL warm-standby async section explicitly identifies committed-but-unshipped loss and commit-to-replay delay.

Live PostgreSQL synchronous-replication section distinguishes remote_write, durable WAL and remote_apply; configured standby counts and unavailable required responses determine waiting and guarantees.

Live MySQL GTID functions document waiting until specified transactions are applied, with timeout/error results. This supports specific progress evidence rather than sleep or average lag for read-your-writes.

Live Cassandra Dynamo architecture documents coordinator fanout, configured response counts, last-write-wins and reconciliation. PostgreSQL sources support leader/follower ordering; topology names alone do not supply fresh or conflict-free reads.
Live PostgreSQL Failover explains preventing old-primary authority, promotion, separate failure-detection software and routing support; merely having a standby is insufficient.

Live PostgreSQL continuous archiving documents base backup plus retained continuous WAL, replay stopping at a chosen time and archival testing. A current replica can replicate accidental deletion; historical restore is separate.

Previously live inspected Brewer partition/recovery reasoning plus current PostgreSQL sync costs support explicit operation-level freshness/loss/wait targets, failover tests and restored-history validation.
